name: Prize crossword No 24,605
preamble: Twelve clues have no definition; their answers are of a kind.

clue.text: Tersely discharges soldiers'  protests about introduction of bull

indicators.note: an introduction is the opening, so only the first letter is taken
to be about something is to surround it, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: demos are protest marches
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Troops protesting about a newly arrived bull, and getting dismissed for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Introduction of' picks the first letter. 'Tersely' tells you the definition is a clipped word: DEMOBS is short for demobilises.
explanation.definitionFit: To demob troops is the informal shortening of demobilise, releasing them from military service.

clue.text: City day quarters, ice free

indicators.note: something free of a thing is without it, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for day
quarters are where you live
these three letters are removed from the longer word

explanation.surface: A note about a city's daytime districts being clear of ice.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters I, C and E are not together in RESIDENCE; each is struck out separately, leaving RES and DEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Dresden is a large city in eastern Germany, the capital of Saxony.

clue.text: Mediterranean island capital: sun not hot

indicators.note: one thing given instead of another, 'X not Y', means a letter swap in place

blocks.note: Mahón is the capital of Menorca
standard abbreviation for sun
H for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A travel note on a Mediterranean capital where the sun isn't hot.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the H of MAHON for S. There is no definition: the preamble says twelve answers are of a kind, here actors, and James MASON is one.
explanation.definitionFit: James Mason was the British film actor of Odd Man Out and North by Northwest, fitting the preamble's set of actors.

clue.text: Sportsman - not this one failing to open personal cover

indicators.note: failing to open means having no opening, so the first letter is lost

blocks.note: a bowler in cricket or tenpin
not this one, but that

explanation.surface: A sportsman being told he is not the one who failed to open the batting, with a personal cover thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not this one' is a cute way of saying THAT, which then loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowler hat is a hard round felt hat, a covering a person wears on the head.

clue.text: Off spin is a nightmare for the user

blocks.note: food that is off has gone bad
a spin is a short trip out

explanation.surface: Off-spin bowling is a nightmare for whoever has to use it, in a cricket sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off spin' looks like the cricket term, but it splits into two words. The 'user' is a drug user.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad trip is a frightening hallucinogenic drug experience, a nightmare for someone who takes drugs.

clue.text: Reduced to fit in the sack

indicators.note: to fit in something is to go inside it, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: the sack is slang for bed
reduced means made less

explanation.surface: Something cut down so it will fit inside a sack.
explanation.walkthrough: No definition: Brian BLESSED, the booming-voiced English actor, is one of the preamble's set of actors. 'Hit the sack' means go to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Brian Blessed is a famously loud English stage and screen actor, so he joins the preamble's group of actors.

clue.text: Insult county club

blocks.note: to dis is slang for to insult
Co. is the abbreviation for county

explanation.surface: Someone insulting a county club, such as a cricket side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'County club' reads as one phrase, a county cricket club, but 'club' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a nightclub where people dance to recorded music.

clue.text: Turning assets into cash is on the increase, each pound to be assimilated

indicators.note: something assimilated is absorbed into something larger, so these go inside

blocks.note: rising means increasing
ea. is the abbreviation for each
L for libra, the pound sign

explanation.surface: A financial report: cashing in assets is growing, with every pound absorbed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition and the surface share a money theme, so 'pound' reads as currency; it is the abbreviation L.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise an asset is the accounting term for selling it to convert it into money.

clue.text: Secretary has to settle on a fruit

blocks.note: a PA is a personal assistant
to settle a bill is to pay it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A secretary who must decide on a fruit for lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settle on' reads as choose, but 'settle' means pay and 'on' just places it before the A.
explanation.definitionFit: The papaya is a tropical fruit with orange flesh and black seeds, also called pawpaw.

clue.text: Guardian state

blocks.note: this puzzle appears in the Guardian, so the paper speaks of itself as we
to aver is to state firmly

explanation.walkthrough: No definition: Sigourney WEAVER, the American actor from Alien, is one of the preamble's set. The newspaper refers to itself as WE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigourney Weaver is the American film actor best known for playing Ripley in Alien, so she belongs among the preamble's actors.

clue.text: Misrepresented Lewes's present "Nimby" position

indicators.note: something misrepresented is shown in the wrong form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the Sussex town, taken as letters
present means here, in attendance

explanation.surface: A complaint that the town of Lewes has been wrongly painted as a hotbed of local objectors.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewes is a county town in Sussex, England. The 's stands for 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nimby says 'not in my back yard': build it somewhere other than here, anywhere else.

clue.text: Leader of scout pack

indicators.note: the leader is the one at the front, so take the opening letter

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
to tamp is to pack down firmly

explanation.surface: The person in charge of a pack of Scouts.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as Akela leading the Cubs, but there is no definition: Terence STAMP, the English actor, is one of the preamble's set.
explanation.definitionFit: Terence Stamp was the English film actor of Far from the Madding Crowd and Superman II, fitting the preamble's group.

clue.text: Fish without fin provided backs off

indicators.note: 'without' in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps round the other
something that backs goes in the opposite direction, so the letters run the other way
off means removed, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: a dace is a small freshwater fish
taken as written
provided that means if

explanation.surface: A fish that has lost a fin, provided it backs away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is the old sense of outside, not lacking. No definition: Charles DANCE, the English actor from Game of Thrones, is one of the preamble's set.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Dance is the English actor known for Game of Thrones, placing him in the preamble's set of actors.

clue.text: Woman's so perversely into football team's tackiness

indicators.note: perversely suggests going the contrary way, so the letters run backwards
to go into something is to sit inside it

blocks.note: Vi is a woman's name, plus the possessive S
taken as written
City, as in Manchester City, is a common football team name

explanation.surface: A woman perversely signing up to a football team's tacky image.
explanation.walkthrough: Short female names like VI are a staple source of letters. The 's of 'team's' is just the link for the definition that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Viscosity is the stickiness or thickness of a fluid, and tackiness is that same sticky quality.

clue.text: Strong US wind section from Boston or thereabouts

indicators.note: a section from a text is a slice of it, so the letters lie inside the words

blocks.note: found across the end of the first word, the second, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A powerful American wind sweeping through the Boston area.
explanation.walkthrough: The geographic surface fits the definition so well that solvers look for a named wind; the letters sit inside the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A norther is a strong cold wind from the north, especially one blowing over Texas and the Gulf.

clue.text: Call about England's top sporting event being back in business?

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter, so take the opening letter
to be about something is to surround it, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: to call someone is to ring them
the first letter of the word
an open is a tournament anyone can enter, like golf's Open

explanation.surface: A summons over England's premier sporting fixture returning to action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'England's top sporting event' reads as one phrase; it splits into the first letter and the tournament. The question mark flags a loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop or venue reopening is starting to trade again after closure, so it is once more doing business.

clue.text: Hard to make out with wife? Needs sex appeal, idiot!

blocks.note: something dim is hard to see
standard abbreviation for wife
'it' is old slang for sex appeal, as in the It girl

explanation.surface: A man who can't get romantic with his wife is told he needs more sex appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard to make out' is DIM, so 'to make out' belongs to it; 'make out with' reads as kissing but does not here. IT for sex appeal dates from Clara Bow, the It Girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A dimwit is a stupid person, a colloquial synonym for a fool.

clue.text: Some rigging involved American appropriating book

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so these letters are mixed up
to appropriate something is to take it in, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: taken as letters
standard abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A tale of a rigged deal in which an American lifted a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rigging' suggests fixing a result, but it is the ship's ropes. The book's letter joins the American's letters before they are mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: The main brace is the rope controlling the mainsail's yard, part of a sailing ship's rigging.

clue.text: Pro hogs set broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, as seed is sown, so these letters are dispersed
to hog something is to keep hold of it, so one piece grips another

blocks.note: pro means in favour of, for
taken as letters

explanation.surface: A professional monopolising a TV set's broadcasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pro' reads as a professional, but it means FOR. No definition: Jodie FOSTER, the American actor, belongs to the preamble's set.
explanation.definitionFit: Jodie Foster is the American actor of Taxi Driver and The Silence of the Lambs, so she fits the preamble's actors.

clue.text: Filled out again (line having been removed) and rated

indicators.note: removed means taken away, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: to bulk out is to fill out, and RE- makes it again
standard abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A form completed a second time, a line deleted, and then given a grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rated' looks like scored or graded, but it is the old verb to rate, meaning to scold, as in berate.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate someone is an old sense meaning to scold angrily, the same as reprimand.

clue.text: Brow's first furrows

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
furrowed ground is a run of ridges and troughs

explanation.surface: The first lines appearing on a frowning forehead.
explanation.walkthrough: No definition: Jeff BRIDGES, the American actor from The Big Lebowski, is one of the preamble's set.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeff Bridges is the American film actor of The Big Lebowski and Crazy Heart, so he joins the preamble's actors.

clue.text: Composer accepting note should be split

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: J.S. Bach, the German composer
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A composer who agrees that a piece of music ought to be divided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' reads as a verb after 'should be', but it is the noun: a breach is a split or rift.
explanation.definitionFit: A breach is a rift or break in relations between people, the same as a split.

clue.text: Rock star, one turned politician?

indicators.note: to rock is to shake about, so these letters are jolted into a new order

blocks.note: taken as letters
taken as letters

explanation.surface: A rock star who has gone into politics, as several have.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock star' reads as one phrase, but 'Rock' is the signal and 'star' its letters. 'Turned' means became, joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is a member of a senate, an elected legislator and so a kind of politician.

clue.text: Work casually on foreign article

blocks.note: to temp is to do temporary office work
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Doing casual work on a piece from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: No definition: Shirley TEMPLE, the child star of 1930s Hollywood, is one of the preamble's actors.
explanation.definitionFit: Shirley Temple was the hugely popular American child film actor of the 1930s, so she belongs to the preamble's set.

clue.text: Converted believers may be turned outward

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as letters

explanation.surface: Religious converts who might yet turn away again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converted believers' fits the surface so well it reads as converts; 'Converted' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Eversible describes an organ or part that can be everted, that is, pushed inside out.

clue.text: The woman, all female, topless

indicators.note: without a top, so the head letter is removed

blocks.note: the pronoun for a woman
a hen party is a women-only celebration

explanation.surface: A woman at an all-female gathering, without her top.
explanation.walkthrough: A hen night is the British all-women party before a wedding. No definition: Martin SHEEN is one of the preamble's actors.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Sheen is the American actor of Apocalypse Now and The West Wing, fitting the preamble's actors.

clue.text: Transport quite lacking on the way back

indicators.note: travelling back means going in the opposite direction, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: a cab is a taxi
no as in not at all, wholly lacking

explanation.surface: Not enough transport for the return journey.
explanation.walkthrough: Each piece is turned round in place. No definition: Kevin BACON, the American actor, is one of the preamble's set.
explanation.definitionFit: Kevin Bacon is the American film actor of Footloose, famous for the Six Degrees game, so he fits the preamble's actors.

clue.text: Sun up in the outskirts of Cologne

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from bottom to top
outskirts are the edges, so take the outer letters
to be in something is to sit inside it

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the city
Sol is the Latin name for the sun

explanation.surface: The sun rising over the suburbs of Cologne.
explanation.walkthrough: No definition: Glenn CLOSE, the American actor of Fatal Attraction, is one of the preamble's set.
explanation.definitionFit: Glenn Close is the American actor of Fatal Attraction and Dangerous Liaisons, so she belongs to the preamble's actors.

clue.text: Lyricist is after page

blocks.note: p is the abbreviation for page
Tim Rice wrote the lyrics for Evita and Jesus Christ Superstar

explanation.surface: A songwriter chasing a page, perhaps a boy servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the lyricist behind the page. No definition: Vincent PRICE, the horror film actor, is one of the preamble's set.
explanation.definitionFit: Vincent Price was the American actor famed for horror films and the voice on Thriller, fitting the preamble's actors.

clue.text: Be a casual footballer; quit before top level match?

blocks.note: to kick a habit is to quit it
A is the top grade
a bout is a boxing or wrestling match

explanation.surface: A casual player asking whether to give up before a top-flight game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top level match' reads as a premier-league fixture; it splits into the top grade and a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: To kick a ball about is to play football informally, without a proper game or teams.

clue.text: Trap energy inside object like a motorised vehicle

indicators.note: inside means within, so these go within the other piece

blocks.note: an end is an aim or object
a gin is a snare for animals
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A device that captures energy within an object, like the motor of a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' is the noun for a goal, as in 'the object of the exercise', not a thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorised vehicle has an engine fitted, so it is engined, powered by a motor.

clue.text: Hand out gold star (shooting)

blocks.note: to mete out is to hand out
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Awarding a gold star to the shooting team.
explanation.walkthrough: The brackets turn 'star' into 'shooting star', not a reward; the gold star picture is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting star is the everyday name for a meteor burning up as it enters the atmosphere.
